summary: Director Martin Scorsese, 80, was quizzed on internet slang by his daughter Francesca Scorsese in a TikTok posted Thursday 5 October. He correctly guessed terms like "tea", "ick", "no cap" and "slaps", but missed others such as "ship" and "simp", often tying his answers to his films. The video reached one million views and drew amused comments, following Francesca's viral April 2021 video with her father.
one_line: Martin Scorsese, 80, guesses internet slang terms in a viral TikTok quiz by his daughter Francesca, getting several right and drawing a million views.
key_facts: Francesca Scorsese posted the TikTok quiz on Thursday 5 October, in which she asked her father Martin Scorsese, 80, to guess the meaning of internet slang terms.
Scorsese defined "tea" correctly as "you're gonna tell all you know" and "ick" as being "thoroughly repulsed by it".
Scorsese correctly answered "no cap" instantly as "no lying", then asked "How many more of these?"
For "sneaky link", Scorsese guessed personal peccadillos; after Francesca compared it to a "booty call" he said "we never saw specific people in my day".
For "hits different", Francesca used the example "Watching a movie in 70 mm film hits different" and Scorsese described it as perceiving something in a totally different way.
Scorsese guessed "slept on" incorrectly, but Francesca's example "King of Comedy was slept on" referred to his 1983 film starring Robert De Niro, which was a box office flop.
For "ate", Francesca said "Lily Gladstone ate in Killers of the Flower Moon"; Scorsese first said "Consumed the screen" before answering "Ruled."
Scorsese answered "ship" as "A ship is a boat" and defined "simp" as a whining, wimpy person, both incorrect.
Scorsese understood "throw shade" immediately and answered "slaps" as "Obviously, it's good"; for "slay" he guessed "really good?"
The video had been viewed one million times on TikTok, with commenters stunned that he guessed many terms correctly.
In April 2021, Francesca went viral when she asked her father to identify "feminine products" such as an eyelash curler, bobby pins, a hair donut and nipple pasties.
